observation.visible_scene: Extreme close-up of water droplets clinging to a wet transparent surface (glass pane), seen against a bright, out-of-focus white-grey background. The field is densely covered with stationary droplets of many sizes, each showing a small dark refraction/reflection crescent. A faint vertical water streak runs down the centre-left, a faint diagonal streak runs through the lower-left, and a barely visible watermark text sits across the lower-middle. The overall droplet pattern and background stay fixed throughout, indicating no camera pan or zoom.
visible_changes: A thin dark trail along the central vertical streak lengthens downward: a dark dash first appears near the upper part of the streak around t=0.2 s and its lower end advances to roughly the middle of the streak by t=0.6 s, then persists (a droplet sliding down the streak, leaving a darker wet path behind it).

A thin dark trail along the lower-left diagonal streak grows steadily downward across the whole excerpt, its dark segment extending from the upper part of that streak toward the bottom edge (a second droplet running down the glass).
The vast majority of individual droplets keep the same position and shape from the first to the last sampled frame; only the two running trails change appreciably.
Subtle shifts in the dark highlight/reflection inside a few droplets near the active streaks accompany the moving water, but these are reflections within the same drops, not new objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the droplets to start running (e.g. a wipe, added water, gravity threshold) is not shown.
Whether the central trail's motion truly stops or merely slows beyond the last frame is unknown.
Whether the diagonal trail reaches the bottom edge and exits the view is not captured.
The state of the scene before t=0 and after the final frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: Exact pixel positions of the trail endpoints are approximate due to the low contrast of the dark lines against the bright background.
It is uncertain whether the central running droplet halts or continues very slowly after about t=0.6 s.

Possible very minor camera drift cannot be confirmed or denied because the static background provides no clear reference; the stationary droplets appear fixed, suggesting no significant camera motion.

and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
